Fortín Toledo is associated with conservation work in the Chaco. The local center studies and protects the tagua, or Chacoan peccary. Learning about this animal offers a close look at a distinctive inhabitant of the dry forests and helps explain why protecting the region's natural habitats matters.

The center is located in the Filadelfia area and complements visits to lagoons and forest landscapes. Here the nature-focused part of the journey has a specific theme: the animal, its habitat and the people working to conserve the species. Fortín Toledo reveals the Chaco through its wildlife and an active conservation project.

Iguaçu Falls are located on the Iguaçu River near the border between Brazil and Argentina. The main itinerary follows viewpoints and trails in the national park, including the route to the Devil's Throat.

You can add Macuco Safari, the Bird Park, a boat trip and a panoramic helicopter flight on the Brazilian side. If you want to see Iguaçu from both Brazil and Argentina, it is best to allow enough time for both sides from the outset.

Francisco Coloane Marine Park lies in the Strait of Magellan among the islands and fjords of southern Chilean Patagonia. It is a protected whale feeding area.

Vessel routes follow the park's coastline. From the water, travelers may spot humpback or sei whales, as well as dolphins, sea lions and seabirds. Wildlife sightings depend on natural conditions.

A trip here offers the chance to observe marine wildlife against a backdrop of low island shores and the mountains of Tierra del Fuego. Visits on cruise itineraries involve sailing along the coast.

The history of Fray Bentos is closely tied to the Liebig company and the Anglo Uruguay refrigerated meat-processing plant. The surviving industrial complex shows how the factory's operations shaped the town and the wider region.

At the Anglo Museum, you can explore this history through the former production facilities and exhibits. The Fray Bentos Industrial Landscape is listed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
